body_en: The teaching chair for the commentary on the Forty Hadith of al-Nawawi · Course on the law of inheritance shares (farāʾiḍ) · Course on the language sciences · Course on Islamic transactions (muʿāmalāt) · The Sharia Sciences Series · Course on the rulings of the prayer, in Hassaniyya · Commentary on the text of al-Rahbiyyah · Course commenting on the book al-Akhlaq wa-l-Siyar · Course commenting on the book Miftah al-Wusul

flags.note: This is not a text by the Sheikh. It is the index page of the Courses section: nine course titles that are link labels in the site's navigation, with no connecting prose. It passes the 200-character test only because there are nine of them. It should not be rendered as an article. It is nonetheless useful as a catalogue of the course series, and it confirms the section that IDs 660-665 belong to, since 'سلسلة العلوم الشرعية' appears in it.

flags.note: Two typographical errors in the source: 'دروة' and 'درورة' for 'دورة'. Both are left as served in body_ar and read as intended in the English, recorded rather than silently corrected per style guide section 11. Because these are link labels, the errors are likely to be reproducible in the site's own menu data and worth reporting to the Sheikh's office as a site defect rather than a corpus one.

translator_notes: The separating middle dots in the English are editorial: the source has no separators at all between the titles, which run together as plain text once the menu markup is stripped. Without them the English would be unreadable. No words have been added.
'كرسي' is the endowed teaching chair, rendered 'teaching chair'.

al-Rahbiyyah is the standard didactic poem on inheritance shares; al-Akhlaq wa-l-Siyar is Ibn Hazm's work on ethics; Miftah al-Wusul is al-Tilimsani's work on legal theory. Titles are left romanised, as citations. The Sheikh does not name the authors here and none have been added to the body.
